easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord rides upon a swift cloud and comes into Egypt.
easy.q: Who comes into Egypt at the beginning of the passage?

answers: They are moved at the Lord’s presence
easy.explanation: The idols of Egypt are moved when the Lord appears.
easy.q: What happens to the idols of Egypt?

easy.explanation: The Lord gives Egypt over into the hand of a cruel lord.
easy.q: Into whose hand is Egypt given?

medium.explanation: The passage describes brother fighting brother, city fighting city, and kingdom fighting kingdom.
medium.q: What does “I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians” describe?

answers: They seek idols, charmers, and wizards
medium.explanation: After the counsel is destroyed, they seek idols, charmers, familiar spirits, and wizards.
medium.q: What do the Egyptians do when their counsel fails?

medium.explanation: The failing spirit is connected with Egypt’s confusion and collapse.
medium.q: What does it mean that the spirit of Egypt shall fail?

challenge.explanation: The passage moves from internal conflict to failed counsel and finally to harsh rule.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes Egypt’s collapse?

answers: The idols are powerless before the Lord
The idols save Egypt from war
challenge.explanation: The idols’ movement at the Lord’s presence shows their inability to help Egypt.
challenge.q: What does the movement of the idols emphasize?

challenge.explanation: The divided condition of Egypt is followed by its being ruled by a fierce king.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from internal conflict to a fierce king’s rule?

paragraphs.title: The Drying Nile and the Collapse of Livelihoods

easy.explanation: The waters fail, and the river is wasted and dried up.
easy.q: What happens to the waters in this passage?

easy.explanation: The verse says that the reeds and flags shall wither.
easy.q: What happens to the reeds and flags?

easy.explanation: The passage mentions fishers, those who cast angles, flax workers, weavers, and makers of sluices and ponds.
easy.q: Who suffers because of the water crisis?

medium.explanation: The fishers mourn, those who cast angle lament, and those who spread nets languish.
medium.q: How does the drying of the waters affect the fishers?

medium.explanation: Those who work in fine flax and weave networks are described as confounded.
medium.q: How are the flax workers and weavers affected?

medium.explanation: The context shows that the nets are used for fishing.
medium.q: What is a net in the phrase “they that spread nets upon the waters”?

answers: The waters support fishing, plants, and several trades
The waters have no connection with work
challenge.explanation: The loss of water damages fishing, vegetation, flax work, weaving, and water systems.
challenge.q: What is the central connection between the drying waters and the loss of livelihoods?

answers: Flax workers, weavers, and water-system builders are also mentioned
challenge.explanation: The passage lists several occupations affected by the drying waters.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the damage affects more than fishermen?

answers: The crisis affects both nature and the society dependent on it
The crisis concerns only one person
The waters become a source of abundance
challenge.explanation: The passage connects environmental collapse with the collapse of many livelihoods.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the repeated references to rivers, plants, and workers?

paragraphs.title: The Failure of Wisdom and Leadership

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Surely the princes of Zoan are fools.”
easy.q: How are the princes of Zoan described?

easy.explanation: The princes and counsellors have deceived and seduced Egypt.
The Lord mingles a perverse spirit in the midst of Egypt.
easy.q: What does the Lord mingle in Egypt?

answers: Their counsel is brutish and they mislead Egypt
medium.explanation: Their counsel has become brutish, and they have led Egypt astray.
medium.q: Why is the wisdom of Pharaoh’s counsellors useless?

medium.explanation: The Egyptians are caused to err in every work, like a drunken man staggering.
medium.q: What is the result of the perverse spirit?

medium.explanation: In this context, brutish means foolish, senseless, or lacking wisdom.
medium.q: What does “brutish” mean in “the counsel ... is become brutish”?

answers: Bad leadership improves the people’s lives
Leadership has no effect on Egypt
challenge.explanation: The rulers and counsellors mislead Egypt, leaving the nation unable to act rightly.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage show between bad leadership and the nation’s condition?

answers: They claim wisdom but are called fools
They have no connection with government
challenge.explanation: They claim to be sons of the wise, but the text calls their counsel brutish.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the counsellors’ claim and the prophet’s description?

answers: No part of Egypt can carry out effective work
Everyone in Egypt becomes a leader
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that neither the leaders nor the people can accomplish effective work.
challenge.q: What does “the head or tail, branch or rush” suggest in this context?

answers: The shaking hand of the Lord
easy.explanation: Egypt fears because of the shaking of the hand of the Lord of hosts.

answers: As a source of joy only
easy.explanation: The land of Judah shall be a terror unto Egypt.
easy.q: How does the land of Judah appear to Egypt?

answers: They speak the language of Canaan and swear to the Lord
easy.explanation: Five cities in Egypt speak the language of Canaan and swear to the Lord of hosts.
easy.q: What do five Egyptian cities do?

answers: It is connected with the counsel of the Lord
medium.explanation: Everyone who mentions Judah is afraid because of the Lord’s counsel concerning Egypt.
medium.q: Why does Judah cause Egypt to fear?

answers: A change in their identity and relationship to the Lord
medium.explanation: The cities are described as adopting Canaan’s language and swearing to the Lord.
medium.q: What does the description of cities speaking Canaan’s language suggest?

medium.explanation: The verse explains that mentioning Judah causes Egyptians to fear.
medium.q: What does “terror” mean in the statement that Judah shall be a terror unto Egypt?

answers: Judah becomes a source of fear and influence
challenge.explanation: Egypt fears even the mention of the land of Judah.
challenge.q: What change in Egypt’s attitude toward Judah is described?

answers: Fear of the Lord’s hand appears alongside a movement toward Him
Fear removes every relationship with the Lord
The Lord is mentioned only in connection with work
challenge.explanation: Egypt fears the Lord’s hand, while the cities speak Canaan’s language and swear to Him.
challenge.q: How are fear and speech about the Lord connected in these verses?

answers: Fear is accompanied by religious and linguistic change
The passage denies any change in Egypt
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from fear to cities expressing allegiance to the Lord.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from Egypt’s fear to cities swearing to the Lord?

paragraphs.title: Recognition of the Lord and Healing for Egypt

easy.explanation: The passage says there shall be an altar to the Lord in the midst of Egypt.
easy.q: What is established in the land of Egypt?

easy.explanation: They cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors.
easy.q: To whom do the Egyptians cry because of their oppressors?

easy.explanation: The Lord is entreated of them and heals them.
easy.q: What does the Lord do after the Egyptians return to Him?

answers: A sign and a witness unto the Lord
medium.explanation: The altar and pillar serve as a sign and witness unto the Lord of hosts.
medium.q: What are the altar and pillar described as?

answers: Crying, deliverance, knowing the Lord, returning, and healing
medium.explanation: The passage describes Egypt crying to the Lord, being delivered, knowing Him, returning, and being healed.
medium.q: What sequence is described concerning Egypt?

medium.explanation: The Lord smites Egypt and then heals it as the people return to Him.
medium.q: What does “smite and heal” mean in this passage?

answers: The striking leads Egypt to return to the Lord, and healing follows
Healing happens without relation to the Lord
challenge.explanation: The passage presents striking, returning, being entreated, and healing as connected events.
challenge.q: How are the striking and healing related?

answers: Crying to Him, sacrifice, vows, and returning to Him
challenge.explanation: The Egyptians cry to the Lord, sacrifice, make vows, know Him, and return to Him.
challenge.q: What does recognition of the Lord include in these verses?

answers: Egypt moves from calamity to recognizing and being healed by the Lord
Egypt moves from strength to conquest
Egypt moves from farming to seafaring
challenge.explanation: The chapter moves from judgment and fear to recognition, repentance, and healing.
challenge.q: What major change occurs in Egypt in this chapter?

paragraphs.title: A Way of Peace and Blessing Among the Nations

easy.explanation: The passage says there shall be a highway out of Egypt to Assyria.
easy.q: Between which countries is a highway established?

easy.explanation: Israel is described as the third with Egypt and Assyria.
easy.q: Who joins Egypt and Assyria as a third?

answers: A blessing in the midst of the land
easy.explanation: The three are included together in blessing.
easy.q: What do the three nations become together?

answers: Connection and movement between the nations
medium.explanation: The highway allows the Egyptians and Assyrians to travel and serve together.
medium.q: What does the highway between Egypt and Assyria represent?

answers: It joins them as a third
medium.explanation: Israel is the third with Egypt and Assyria and shares in the blessing.
medium.q: How is Israel included in the blessing of Egypt and Assyria?

answers: The people who belong to the Lord
medium.explanation: The Lord calls Israel His inheritance, indicating His special possession and relationship.
medium.q: What does “mine inheritance” mean when applied to Israel?

answers: A movement toward shared travel and blessing
challenge.explanation: The highway and shared blessing portray cooperation among Egypt, Assyria, and Israel.
challenge.q: What change in relations among the nations is described at the end?

answers: Israel shares in the relationship alongside Egypt and Assyria
Egypt and Assyria have no connection with Israel
challenge.explanation: Israel is counted alongside the other two nations as a partner in blessing.
challenge.q: What does calling Israel “the third” emphasize?

answers: After judgment and healing, the passage describes peace and blessing among nations
It returns only to the water crisis
It describes another failure of the counsellors
challenge.explanation: The chapter concludes with a transformed relationship among the nations under the Lord’s blessing.
challenge.q: How does the ending connect with the earlier ideas of the chapter?
